title: Theo's "2%" Credit Card Costs $1,200 a Year 😂
description:
Theo spots "only 2%" on his credit card and works out that his $5,000 balance costs a hundred bucks a year. Nora reads the small print: that's 2% a MONTH. So $100 every month, $1,200 a year, a 24% APR, and if he only pays the interest he still owes the full $5,000.

The number that matters is the APR, because a monthly rate always looks small.

What's your card's APR? Go check, then tell us below 👇

Follow for more numbers that change how you spend.

⚠️ Illustration with fictional characters: $5,000 balance, 2% monthly rate, interest paid monthly, no fees. Simplified: real cards charge interest daily and require minimum payments. US average card rate of 22.36% is for accounts assessed interest, Aug 2026 (preliminary), Federal Reserve G.19 released 7 Oct 2026. This is not financial advice.
